source_excerpt: Jonathan Taylor has not asked to leave Indianapolis, but he knows the decision may not be his. The Colts running back addressed the trade talk Thursday, saying he remains proud to wear the horseshoe while accepting that circumstances can change. His comments arrive as the Washington Commanders emerge as a possible destination before the November 10 deadline. Washington needs help after a difficult start, while Indianapolis has already moved two prominent veterans. Taylor offered no indication he wants out, but his answer left his future open at a pivotal point in the season.Jonathan Taylor leaves the door open without asking outâI havenât heard anything, and I canât control that, obviously,â Taylor said. âIâm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. And similar to Quenton [Nelson] and [DeForest Buckner], they were proud to wear the horseshoe, they were proud to be here. But obviously, circumstances may cause otherwise. So, hopefully that day may not come, but I canât control that.âTaylor was not requesting a trade. He was acknowledging that loyalty does not always decide a player's future. His reference to Nelson and Buckner carried weight: Indianapolis moved both veterans earlier this week.Nelson went to Seattle for a third-round and fifth-round pick, while Buckner was sent to San Francisco for a future fourth-round selection. Those deals have made it harder to rule out another major departure.Commanders have a reason to make a moveWashington enters Week 8 at 1-4-1, sitting 2.5 games behind the NFC East lead after its bye. The Commanders need to give quarterback Jayden Daniels more support, particularly with another season of his rookie-contract window at risk. A move for an established running back could help, though it would not fix every issue on the roster.ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Matt Bowen listed 25 potential trade candidates on October 28 and ranked Taylor first. They named Washington among five possible destinations, alongside Denver, Minnesota, New Orleans and Seattle.Fowler reported that teams he had spoken with were not convinced Indianapolis would trade Taylor, despite heavy interest. He pointed to Kenneth Walker III's move to Kansas City as an example of how a premier running back can quickly change a team's outlook. Fowler also noted that the Colts' difficult season could trigger further movement.Colts would need a major returnTaylor is 27 and a three-time Pro Bowler. Indianapolis would have little reason to accept a modest offer for a player of his standing. A second-round pick, perhaps with another selection attached, would be a reasonable starting point. A first-rounder could also be the asking price, but that remains speculation, not a confirmed Colts demand.Taylor would give Washington a proven runner and another option to ease the burden on Daniels. The Commanders would still have to decide whether the price makes sense with other roster needs to address.Taylor's comments did not suggest he expects to leave Indianapolis. They showed that he understands he cannot control the team's plans. After the Nelson and Buckner trades, that distinction is no longer theoretical.
